instruction:
Fix `plugins/catalog/src/components/CatalogEntityPage/useEntityFromUrl.ts` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. major (line 53): `const requestedRef = stringifyEntityRef({ kind, namespace, name })` runs unconditionally on every render, above every guard. `useRouteRefParams` is just `useParams()` cast (packages/core-plugin-api/src/routing/useRouteRefParams.ts:28), so `kind`/`namespace` can be undefined — the pre-existing code tolerates that case explicitly via the `if (!name)` effect that posts an error and navigates to '/'. `stringifyEntityRef` does `kind.toLowerCase()` with no guard (packages/catalog-model/src/entity/ref.ts:157), so an absent `kind` now throws a TypeError during render instead of reaching the existing error path. This violates the fail-closed requirement that the lookup/render path never throws (AC-20). — fix: Compute `requestedRef` lazily and defensively, e.g. `const requestedRef = kind && namespace && name ? stringifyEntityRef({ kind, namespace, name }) : undefined;` and add `!requestedRef` to the resolution gate and the redirect effect, so a malformed/absent param set falls back to the existing missing-name behaviour rather than throwing.
2. major (line 57): The resolution gate reads `loading`/`entity` from the direct lookup without checking that they belong to the ref currently being requested, so the binding rule 'resolution may only be attempted after a direct lookup has already missed' does not hold after the redirect. The route (`/catalog/:namespace/:kind/:name/*`) does not remount, so after `navigate(..., { replace: true })` the params change while `entity` is still the stale `undefined` and `loading` still the stale `false` from the old ref's lookup; `attemptedRefRef.current` is the old ref, so the gate passes and a second `resolveFormerEntityRef` query is issued for the destination ref before its own direct lookup has settled. With two entities each declaring the other's current ref as a former ref this chains redirects. Additionally, the redirect `useEffect` depends on `location.pathname/search/hash`, which change as a result of its own `navigate`, while `resolution.value` is still `'resolved'` — producing a second `navigate` to the same URL on the next commit. — fix: Tag the direct lookup result with the ref it was fetched for (e.g. have the `useAsyncRetry` body return `{ ref: requestedRef, entity }`) and gate resolution on `settled.ref === requestedRef && !settled.entity`; and guard the redirect effect so it navigates at most once per resolved value (e.g. a `navigatedRefRef` holding the formerEntityRef already acted on), rather than re-deriving the target from a location its own navigation mutated.
